question: How should Claude Code's hooks reach log's code?

options.name: Bun per hook through Git Bash
options.description: What runs today: each hook is `bun "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/scripts/hooks/<name>.ts"` through Git Bash, a new process per hook per event.

options.name: Bun per hook, exec form
options.description: Each hook stays a separate Bun process, started directly with `command` + `args`, no shell.

options.name: One Bun process per event
options.description: One exec-form Bun process per event runs every hook's logic for that event in-process and prints one combined answer.

options.name: http hook per event to the warm service
options.description: Every hook becomes one `type: "http"` hook per event to the long-lived context service on 127.0.0.1:47317, which answers all of that event's hooks from its open state in one request.

options.name: http for context, exec form for the refusing hooks
options.description: As D for hooks that add context, but the two refusing PreToolUse hooks (chatNames, liveLogs) stay exec-form Bun processes so they still refuse when the service is down; alert-only output may use asyncRewake.

question: How should log's Bun side reach the Python engines?

options.name: Python per call, relaying to a host
options.description: Today for X and Instagram: a new Python process per call connects to the account's long-lived host over a new loopback TCP connection and relays one request.

options.name: Python per call, no host
options.description: Today for Discord, Slack and Reddit: a new Python process per call does the work itself.

options.name: Bun to the host directly, new TCP connection per call
options.description: Bun reads the host's port and token and opens a new loopback TCP connection per call, newline JSON, no Python relay. Every platform gets a host.

options.name: Bun to the host directly, kept-open connection
options.description: As C, but each Bun process keeps one connection per host open, with request ids, line reassembly and reconnect on host restart; the host reads many requests per connection.

options.name: stdio pipe to a child host owned by the MCP server
options.description: Each MCP server starts the hosts as its own children and talks over stdio pipes.

options.name: Windows named pipe to the host
options.description: Bun reaches an independent host over a Windows named pipe instead of TCP.

options.name: AF_UNIX socket to the host
options.description: Bun reaches an independent host over a Unix-domain socket (Windows 10+).

options.name: Shared memory to the host
options.description: Bun and the host exchange messages through a shared memory mapping plus an event or semaphore.

options.name: Port the clients to TypeScript
options.description: Remove Python by porting twikit, instagrapi, endcord and gabriel into Bun.
